statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-88647: GnuTLS hostname verification can fall back to the certificate's subject Common Name when the subjectAltName holds an SRV otherName (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.7) whose value is an OCTET STRING instead of an IA5String: the entry fails to decode, keeps the generic otherName type, and so does not suppress the Common Name fallback that the CVE-2026-42012 fix added for well-formed SRV names (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-88647, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1802; reproduced against Debian's 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 in https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/work_items/1965). The GnuTLS maintainers dispute it as outside the threat model in their SECURITY.md, because a CA the user trusts has to issue the certificate, and have filed a dispute with the CVE program (same issue); Debian lists gnutls28 in trixie as unfixed (unimportant): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-88647. No upstream release fixes it; a proposed change that keeps the SRV type when the value fails to decode is open and not merged (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/merge_requests/2165). The DHI gnutls28 packages for Debian 13 are built from Debian's 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 source, and none of the changes DHI adds touches subject alternative name decoding or hostname verification, so the published builds behave as reported. Pending: a maintainer decision on whether the upstream trust-boundary dispute holds for every image that uses this package, or whether to ship a fix once one is accepted upstream.
